subject: SummitWood on-prem hotpath: latency spike and error cascade
messages:
From: Emily Park <epark@summitwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: SummitWood SRE Team <sre@summitwood.ai>, Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@summitwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unacceptable latency + 5xx spike on private cluster after 11/20 rollout

Marcus / Laura —

We started seeing a major regression after the 11/20 runtime rollout to our on-prem cluster (region: us-west). Metrics from our side:
- p50: 120ms -> 350ms
- p95: 140ms -> 1.2s
- error rate (502/504): from ~0.2% to 4.8% over the last 3 hours
- sustained throughput down ~30% vs baseline

This is impacting our production inference pipelines (inference queue length growing, several downstream inference consumers are timing out). We pulled logs and attached a short diagnostic extract (redwood_diag_20261121.txt). The SRE team flagged a hotpath stall in the attention kernel that coincides with larger batch sizes hitting one node.

We need immediate mitigation and an ETA for resolution. This is high visibility for us — Anna (CISO) has already been looped in from our side. Please advise next steps and whether you recommend a rollback or temporary capacity increase.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of ML Ops, SummitWood AI

Attachments: redwood_diag_20261121.txt (text), screenshots and metric snapshots
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <epark@summitwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, SummitWood SRE Team <sre@summitwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unacceptable latency + 5xx spike on private cluster after 11/20 rollout

Emily —

Thanks for the diagnostics. We see the same signals in our telemetry (INF-2247). Quick alignment and immediate mitigations I'm authorizing now:
1) Start a staggered rollback to the previous kernel variant on 2 of the 6 affected nodes (canary rollback) — ops team on it now.
2) Temporarily increase node concurrency for your VPC (burst capacity) while we validate rollback impact — this will incur overage; we'll track costs and discuss credits.
3) Opened Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2247 with the initial triage notes and the logs you attached.

Please confirm: can your SREs accept a 30-minute maintenance window for the rollback and brief validation? If yes we'll proceed; if not, we will prioritize an instant fallback (auto-route to a compatible warmed model) to reduce 5xxs.

I'm copying Laura for ops/runbook sign-off. I'll stay on this thread and coordinate executive-level updates if needed.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <epark@summitwood.ai>
Cc: SummitWood SRE Team <sre@summitwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unacceptable latency + 5xx spike on private cluster after 11/20 rollout

Emily / Marcus —

Operational plan and checklist attached (rollback_checklist.md). Summary of next steps from ops perspective:
- T+0: Lock new deployments for SummitWood (no further rollouts until safe).
- T+5: Canaried rollback on nodes n1/n3 (reduce batch cap on n2). Monitor p95 and 5xx for 20 minutes.
- T+30: If rollback reduces 5xxs to <1% and p95 < 300ms, proceed with rest of nodes in 2 waves.
- If rollback does not stabilize: initiate model-variant fallback and increase burst capacity by 25%.

Notes on cost / approvals:
- Temporary burst capacity will be billed at the committed overage rate. Marcus, please confirm whether we should auto-authorize up to $6k/day while we validate (I recommend approval for uninterrupted traffic).

Emily — please confirm the maintenance window and whether your SREs can accept the canary nodes (n1/n3) going into rollback at 10:30 PST.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Operational Readiness — Redwood Inference

2) Sales/CS (on separate thread) to prepare a customer credit proposal for SummitWood given this production impact; I'd like a short note for Emily by EOD.

Jonas
